CR-A04: The router (`agent/router.py:90`) sends a prompt to the CP3 programming loop when it names a code file and the programming score reaches 3. A literal-content create is exempt only while the score stays below 5. This prompt scores 5: `implement parser.py` (3), `fix ... failing ... tests` (2) and `failing ... tests` (1). The agent therefore implemented `parser.py` instead of writing `notes.txt` with the given text. The CP1 grader would see a missing `notes.txt` and an unexpected new file.
DL-A12: The agent deleted `a.log` and then exited 1 because `b.log` was missing. That leaves a half-applied change behind an error status. The system prompt (`agent/harness.py:66`) says multi-file deletes are unsupported and should end in an error. The harness lets the first delete happen anyway and gives no rollback when it later finishes with an error. Either outcome alone would be defensible: delete `a.log` and report `b.log` missing, or refuse with nothing deleted. A changed workspace plus a failure exit is neither.
RQ-A01: `read_file` truncates each file at 60,000 characters (`agent/tools.py:10`, `MAX_FILE_CHARS`; truncation at `agent/tools.py:141`). The 84 KB file's answer is on its last line, so the model never sees it. It answers "does not contain any information about blue notebooks" and exits 1. Nothing tells the model to page through the rest. CP1 caps only the summary sources (40 KB); a single read-and-answer file has no stated limit.
RQ-A08: This expectation is debatable. The table has `Notebook | Blue | 12` and `Notebook (damaged) | Blue | 3`. The agent added them and answered 15. The test treats damaged stock as not "currently in stock". Count this as a judgment call rather than a clear bug, but it shows the agent will silently add rows the question did not clearly ask for.
SM-A01: The agent wrote all the bullets on one line (`- logs/start.txt: ... - logs/update.txt: ...`) and dropped the resolution bullet, so the file has 1 line with 2 inline bullets instead of 3 bullet lines. The bullet-count guard (`agent/harness.py:529`) counts bullet markers, not lines, and did not catch the missing third source either. The missing bullet also means the summary omits the actual root cause (the health check).
SM-A02: `guards._parse_limit` (`agent/guards.py:343`) returns the smallest number in any word-limit phrase in the prompt. "each under 40 words" describes the sources, but it still becomes the summary's maximum, overriding the requested 50 to 80. The summary came out at 34 words.
SM-A03: The number guard `guards.unsupported_numbers` (`agent/guards.py:486`, called at `agent/harness.py:557`) rejects any number in a summary that does not appear verbatim in the sources. The prompt asks for the total outage minutes (12 + 18 + 15 = 45). The guard rejects 45, and the agent exits 1 with "The summary contains a calculated value (45) that was not explicitly present in the source files". No summary is written.
CX-12: This is the same failure class as the four failed hidden cases in the hw1-2 report, and the audit-fix change does not cover it. `_about_files()` (`agent/harness.py:706`) treats a turn as file work when it matches `_FILE_ACTION` (`agent/harness.py:50`), unless a memory phrase (`_MEMORY`, line 47) matches first. "The new status for record 104 should be 'shipped'. Don't change anything yet." has no memory phrase and contains the verb *change*, even negated. The no-op guard at `agent/harness.py:647-650` then refuses success on this first turn (no history), and the second refusal ends the run with exit 1: "The task cannot be performed as no operation was carried out." Turn 2 still worked, but the case fails on turn 1.
CX-15: This fails before the model is ever called. `_no_referent()` (`agent/harness.py:176-193`) treats a first turn as a follow-up with nothing to refer to when three things hold: it matches `_FOLLOWUP` (`agent/harness.py:37`, which includes the bare word *total*), it names no file, and it contains a data verb (*total* again). "My total budget for the Lisbon trip is 1200 euros." meets all three, so turn 1 exits 1 with "This request refers to something from an earlier turn, but this conversation has no earlier turns...". Any first-turn statement that uses total, average, sum or mean, plus a word like it/this/that or a data verb, is rejected the same way.
CV-A06: `csvtools.compare` (`agent/csvtools.py:190-205`) falls back to case-insensitive string ordering when a cell is not numeric (line 201). For `quantity > 100`, it compares `"n/a" > "100"` as strings, which is true, so the `N/A` row was removed with the large quantities. Non-numeric cells should never match a numeric comparison.
CV-A16: `compare` checks equality numerically whenever both sides parse as numbers (`agent/csvtools.py:195-198`), so ID `007` equals `7`, and `csv_update_cell` updates every match. The row with ID `7` was changed to `done` along with `007`. IDs are identifiers, not quantities, and need an exact string match.
CV-A17: Dates are not parsed, so `before March 1, 2026` against `M/D/YYYY` cells becomes a string comparison. `10/2/2026` sorts before `3/1/2026` as text and was removed, even though October 2026 is after March 2026. ISO dates happen to work; any other date format gives wrong results without any warning.
PG-D: Requirement 8 failed: `count --invalid` always prints 0. On the second run, requirement 7 also failed (`total --json` printed `"category": null`). The harness checks only run the task's own example commands plus generic probes (`agent/deep.py`). A flag mentioned only in requirement prose (`count --invalid`, `{"invalid": N}`) is never executed, and the agent finished with time left.
PG-E: The agent wrote `tally.py` in one call, made a one-line edit, and declared success after 3 model calls and 83 s, with about 200 s of its 285 s budget unused. Its program rejects `$12.00` / `+12.00` / `-$3.50` amounts as invalid and ignores surrounding whitespace rules (requirements 10 and 11). Because of that, even the official requirements 1-6 come out wrong on this data, and the `--from/--to`, category-list and `bottom` features were never implemented. The harness reported "No problems detected" because it only exercises example commands and generic probes, so nothing checked the six requirements that have no example command.
DB-1: Both branches fail one or two keys for the same reason: the type rules in `agent/taskspec.py:83-105`. `orders_error_code` ends in `_code`, which `_INT_SUFFIX` (line 89) forces to an integer, but the logged error code is the string `INV_HOLD_TIMEOUT`. `report_set` then rejects the correct value as the wrong type, and the model fills in a number from the same line (`waited_ms`) or gives up. `payment_amount_cents` has no integer suffix, and its description mentions *intent*, which `_STR_HINT` maps to string. The correct number is therefore written as `"68707"`. The same two keys failed on both audit-fix runs and on every seed (DB-1/2/3), so this is deterministic, not model noise: about 2 of 12 debugging points lost whenever a hidden key is a string-valued `*_code` or a count-like `*_cents`/`*_amount`.
DB-2: This uses renamed service files (edge/checkout/stock/billing) and order ORD-58212. On audit-fix, `lock_name` came back as `reservation` instead of `sku-ledger#8`, and the type rule from DB-1 turned `payment_amount_cents` into a string. The agent's final message admits `orders_error_code: WRONG TYPE: must be a JSON integer`. On 86a82b, `payment_intent_id` and `payment_amount_cents` were left empty: the payments log is JSON lines with `intent`/`order_ref` keys, and the agent never linked them to the order.
DB-3: `root_cause_component` came back as `HoldService`, which is the logger class on the inventory lines, instead of the class that held the lock: `SkuIndexReBuilder` (capital B; `SkuIndexRebuilder` appears in unrelated noise). The nested `Caused by:` chain puts the lock holder in the third exception. The agent stopped at the class named in the log prefix. The same type-rule bug as DB-1 also cost `orders_error_code` and `payment_amount_cents`.
CX-17: This is the CX-12 root cause, triggered by a different verb. "My shopping list for tomorrow has eggs, rice and spinach." contains *list*, which is in `_FILE_ACTION` (`agent/harness.py:50`), and has no `_MEMORY` phrase. `_about_files()` therefore returns true, and the no-op guard (`agent/harness.py:647-650`) refuses the acknowledgement, giving exit 1: "The task cannot be done as there is no file operation required." CX-16 ("copy") happened to pass on audit-fix because the model's first finish was accepted. The guard runs only after a rejected attempt, so passing depends on what the model says first.
CX-18: This is the CX-12/CX-17 root cause, triggered by *read*. "I read about 20 pages of my novel every night." matches `_FILE_ACTION` (`agent/harness.py:50`), so turn 1 is refused as a non-file request (exit 1: "The task cannot be done as it does not involve any file operations..."). Because turn 1 failed, the fact was never acknowledged, and turn 2 answered "The file does not state how many pages you read each night." The model now looks for a file instead of the conversation, so a second turn fails too.
DB-4: This case uses the agent's own development generator with every scenario enabled. It passed 12/12 on one audit-fix run, but scored 10/12 on the second run and 5/12 on a 86a82b run. In the 10/12 run, `payment_intent_id` and `payment_status` were left as empty strings. The payments log uses epoch-millisecond timestamps in this scenario (`mixed_ts`), and the agent finished at 164 s of its 285 s budget with those keys still unset. The run is not stable even on the agent's home ground. The wrap-up writes placeholder blanks instead of continuing the search.

_intro:
111 end-to-end cases (46 CP1, 58 CP2 conversations, 7 CP3 runs) were run live on 2026-10-16/17 against three versions:
- **`fixed`**: this branch. It is `audit-fix` plus the fixes for everything below, and it is the final code.
- **`audit-fix`**: cf57ecf, which includes the CP2 statement-turn fix.
- **`audit-86a82b`**: `claude/agentic-ai-homework-audit-86a82b`, 1eb9054.

## Result after the fixes (`fixed`)

| Area | `audit-fix` | `fixed` |
|---|---|---|
| CP1 (46 cases) | 39 pass | **45 pass**. The one failure is RQ-A08, whose expected answer is debatable. |
| CP2 (58 conversations) | 51 pass | **58 pass** |
| CP3 debugging (4 scenarios × 2 runs) | 9-12/12 | **12/12 on every run** |
| CP3 programming | PG-O 6/6, PG-D 10-11/12, PG-E 1-2/12 | PG-O 6/6, PG-D 11/12, PG-E 1-2/12 (model limit; see the notes) |

Offline suite: 476/476, including 15 new regression unit tests in `tests/unit/test_adversarial_fixes.py`.

## Does the harness match the grader?

The four failed hidden cases from the hw1-2 grading report (GR-01 to GR-04) were also run against the code that was actually graded, the `checkpoint-2` branch. All four fail 3 out of 3, with the same first-turn refusal the report describes (`agent/harness.py:539-541`). The harness reproduces the grader's verdicts.

## What the suite found in `audit-fix` (now fixed unless noted)

1. **The CP2 statement-turn bug is only partly fixed in `audit-fix`.** These first-turn statements are all still refused:
   - "...Don't change anything yet." (CX-12)
   - "My total budget..." (CX-15)
   - "My shopping list..." (CX-17)
   - "I read about 20 pages..." (CX-18)

   Two root causes:
   - `_FILE_ACTION` treats about 30 everyday verbs as file work.
   - `_no_referent` treats *total/average/sum* as a follow-up with nothing to refer to.

   Hidden cases phrased like these would cost the **CP2 context point again**.
2. **CP3 debugging loses about 2 of 12 keys on every seed**, because of the key-type rules in `agent/taskspec.py`:
   - `*_code` is forced to an integer, so the string error code `INV_HOLD_TIMEOUT` is rejected.
   - `payment_amount_cents` is typed as a string.

   A misspelled culprit class behind nested `Caused by:` lines also failed: the agent reported the logger class `HoldService`.
3. **CP3 programming stops early when no harness check fails.** For hidden requirements that have no example command, the agent declared success with about 200 s left:
   - PG-E (`$`/`+` amounts, date filters on every command, category lists, `bottom N`): 1-2/12;
   - PG-D (`count --invalid`): 10-11/12.
4. **CP1 has deterministic failures on harder-than-published inputs:**
   - a create whose content names `parser.py` is routed to the programming loop;
   - reads are truncated at 60k characters;
   - the summary word-limit guard keeps the smallest limit in the prompt;
   - the summary number guard rejects derived totals;
   - a multi-file delete is half-applied before exiting 1.
5. **CSV comparisons:**
   - `N/A` cells compare as text in a numeric filter;
   - ID `007` equals `7`;
   - `M/D/YYYY` dates compare as strings.

Every CP1/CP2 failure below failed **3 of 3 runs**. CP3 runs were done twice, and the misses repeat across runs (see the second-run scores).


## Round 2 (36 new cases aimed at the round-1 fixes)

The round-2 cases have `-B` ids, plus PG-F. They ran on the final code (label `fixed-r2`). **22 of 32 CP1/CP2 cases passed, and all 4 CP3 runs lost points.** Every CP1/CP2 failure repeated 3 out of 3 times, and every CP3 miss repeated on a second run.

New bug classes:
- **Statements opening with a verb-like noun.** "Read receipts...", "List prices..." and "I store my recipes in recipes.txt" are still refused (CX-B01, CX-B03, CX-B05).
- **Word-limit phrasings.** "at most 15 words each", "each under 20 words" and "between 60 and 90 words" are mis-parsed, so summaries are cut short or come out below the minimum (SM-B01/02/03).
- **History compaction.** A fact past character 200 of an older turn is lost (CX-B07).
- **CSV:**
  - day/month dates are read month-first, so every row was deleted with exit 0 (CV-B01);
  - an OR condition removed nothing, with exit 0 (CV-B02);
  - an AND condition was half-applied (CV-B03).
- **CP3 debugging:**
  - the round-1 root-cause check suggests `java.*` frames and stale classes, pushing the model off the right answer (DB-B01);
  - `*_number` keys are forced to integers (DB-B02);
  - the loop guard ends a run at 45 s with an empty report but a **success** status (DB-B03).
- **CP3 programming.** `--json` was ignored on a new command, the export file got a BOM, and on one run `total --category` was broken (PG-F).


## After the round-2 fixes (`final`, the current code)

All 147 cases were run live on the final code. 141 fully pass (CV-B01 passed on its rerun after the direction guard), and the project's own live suite passes 99/99. Offline: 485/485.

- **CP1/CP2: 135 of 136 pass.** The only miss is RQ-A08, whose expected answer is debatable. Every round-2 CP1/CP2 bug is fixed, including CV-B01. On CV-B01 the model inverted "before", and a new direction guard now corrects it.
- **CP3 debugging:**
  - DB-1 to DB-4 and DB-B02 score 12/12 on both runs.
  - DB-B01 scores 10/12 (root cause now right; two extraction slips).
  - DB-B03 scores 10/12 (payment keys; one run hit an endpoint failure).
- **CP3 programming:** PG-O 6/6, PG-D 10/12, PG-F 10/12, PG-E 1/12. The causes of the remaining misses were not all established.
RQ-A08@fixed: The test's expected answer is debatable: damaged notebooks may or may not count as "in stock". The final code adds a guard (D-23) that pushes back once on a number appearing in no file, question, conversation or tool result. It fired here ("your answer states 15, which appears nowhere..."). The model then chose to call `calculate 12 + 3` and answered 15 again. The total is now explicit and auditable instead of invented, and what remains is only the interpretation of "in stock". No other CP1/CP2 case changed with the guard: 103 of 104 pass on the first run, with no flaky cases.
PG-D@fixed: This is now 11/12; requirement 7's `--json` shape is right. Requirement 8 is still missed: `count --invalid` prints 0. The new self-review (`agent/deep.py`, before `FINISH-ACCEPTED`) does make the model test each requirement, but it tests with a clean CSV that has no invalid rows, so the zero looks plausible to it. This remains a model-capability limit.
PG-E@fixed: This is still 0-1/12. The self-review now fires twice, and the model runs 8 commands against its own test CSV. That CSV contains no `$`/`+` amounts, no padded fields and no date filters, so every check "passes". Turning prose requirements into test inputs is beyond what this model does reliably. Generating requirement-specific probes in the harness would mean task-specific knowledge, which the design avoids (D-14). This is a stress variant.
DB-1@fixed: The first run on the fixed code hit an endpoint outage: `HTTP 503 Server is busy` repeated for 64 s, from 49 s to 113 s, and the wrap-up kept the keys set so far (7/12). The second run scored 11/12, with `lock_name` set to the culprit class. The final code adds a check for that: a lock key may not hold one of the cause classes, and the message names the lock from the linked `Caused by:` line.
SM-B01@fixed-r2: "3 bullet points of at most 15 words each" puts *each* after the limit. `_per_item_spans` (`agent/guards.py:363`) only recognises "each bullet ... N words" (each before the noun), so 15 becomes a limit on the whole file. Trimming then cut the summary to 2 short bullets and dropped the load-balancer cause. This is a regression in my round-1 fix: it handles only one word order.
SM-B02@fixed-r2: "in exactly 3 sentences, each under 20 words": "each under" has no item noun after *each*, so it parses as a 19-word total. The 3 sentences were squeezed into 18 words.
SM-B03@fixed-r2: "between 60 and 90 words": `parse_word_min` (`agent/guards.py:408`) matches "N to M" and "N-M" but not "between N and M", so no minimum is enforced. The summary came out at 34 words.
CX-B01@fixed-r2: "Read receipts are turned on for my phone." opens with *Read*, which `_IMPERATIVE` (`agent/harness.py:56`) treats as a command. `is_statement()` returns False, the turn counts as file work, and the no-op guard refuses it (exit 1). Turn 2 then fails too, because the fact was never stored as acknowledged.
CX-B03@fixed-r2: "List prices at my store went up by 5 percent this month." opens with *List*, the same root cause as CX-B01. Both turns exit 1.
CX-B05@fixed-r2: "I store my recipes in recipes.txt on my laptop." names a file, so `is_statement()` is False at once (`guards.prompt_paths`), and *store* is in `_FILE_ACTION`. The statement is refused (exit 1). The recall in turn 2 still works.
CX-B07@fixed-r2: Older turns are compacted to their first 200 characters (`agent/session.py:335`; `RECENT_TURNS = 8`, line 42). The policy number is at about character 330 of turn 1. The model's acknowledgement was just "Noted: travel details provided.", so after 10 turns the number is gone: "not mentioned in the conversation history". The seat (14C, within the first 200 characters) was still recalled.
CV-B01@fixed-r2: The prompt says the dates are day/month/year, and the model passed the value `10/3/2026`. `parse_date` (`agent/csvtools.py:203`) tries `%m/%d/%Y` first, which reads October 3, so all 4 rows were deleted and the run still reported success. It also reads `05/03/2026` as May 3 but `15/03/2026` as 15 March, which is inconsistent within one file. Removing every row also passed without any sanity check.
CV-B02@fixed-r2: The model called `csv_delete_rows` with `contains "cancelled refunded"` in a single call. That matched 0 rows, so an unchanged copy was saved, and the agent still returned success with "were not found". The tool takes one condition. Nothing pushes the model to make one call per value, and nothing flags "0 rows removed" for a request that clearly expects removals.
CV-B03@fixed-r2: "qty is 0 and status is pending" became `qty == 0` only, so B (0, shipped) was wrongly removed. The tool has no AND condition, and the harness doesn't notice that half of the condition was dropped.
PG-F@fixed-r2: Run 1 scored 10/12. `monthly --json` ignored `--json` and printed the tab format (requirement 8), and `export` wrote the file with a UTF-8 BOM (`\ufeffcategory,total`, requirement 11). Run 2 scored 8/12: `total --category` ignored the category entirely, printing the grand total, which breaks requirements 3, 5 and 6, all official. The self-review step ran but did not catch either problem.
DB-B01@fixed-r2: This is a regression in my round-1 root-cause check (`Report.cause_candidates`, `agent/report.py:97`). For a non-lock cause it takes the first frame under the innermost `Caused by`, which is `java.util.concurrent.FutureTask`. It also lists the class from the older, recovered stall on the same worker (`CouponBatchLoader`). The correct `SupplierFeedClient` was flagged "CHECK: not the class the failure chain blames", and the model switched to `CouponBatchLoader` on both runs. Run 1 also took the CREATED line's timestamp instead of the QUEUED one, and the orders timeout (20000) instead of the feed's (25000).
DB-B02@fixed-r2: `order_number` ends in `_number`, which `_INT_SUFFIX` (`agent/taskspec.py:89`) forces to an integer. The logged value is the string `ORD-77341`, so `report_set` coerced it to 77341 on both runs.
DB-B03@fixed-r2: Run 1 scored 0/12. The model repeated `grep "POST /api/checkout -> 502 Bad Gateway"` with `max_matches: 1` eight times. The loop guard (`agent/deep.py:835`, `force_wrap` at 8 identical calls) ended the run at 45 s, out of a 285 s budget, with **no key set**, and the run still reported `result: success` with an all-placeholder REPORT.json. Run 2 (9/12) picked the logger class `HoldService` and left the payment keys empty. The retried upstream trace itself was handled correctly.
RQ-A08@final: The test's expected answer is debatable: damaged notebooks may or may not count as "in stock". The final code adds a guard (D-23) that pushes back once on a number appearing in no file, question, conversation or tool result. It fired here ("your answer states 15, which appears nowhere..."). The model then chose to call `calculate 12 + 3` and answered 15 again. The total is now explicit and auditable instead of invented, and what remains is only the interpretation of "in stock". No other CP1/CP2 case changed with the guard: 103 of 104 pass on the first run, with no flaky cases.
PG-D@final: 10/12 on both runs. Requirement 8 (`count --invalid`) is still missing, and requirement 7's `total --category --json` shape was wrong this time. The self-review now also shows the commands' current output, but the model did not act on the mismatch. This is a model-capability limit, and there is no task-specific harness logic by design (D-14).
PG-E@final: 1/12 on both runs: a stress variant. The model's tally rejects `$`/`+` amounts and ignores several flags. The same limit as before, not a harness bug.
PG-F@final: 10/12 on both runs, up from 8–10. `monthly --json` still prints the tab-separated format, and `export` writes a UTF-8 BOM. Both were visible in the self-review's command outputs, but the model did not fix them. This is a model-capability limit.
DB-B01@final:
10/12 on both runs, up from 9/11. The root cause is now right (`SupplierFeedClient`) on both runs; the repaired check no longer suggests `java.*` frames or the older stall. Two extraction mistakes remain:
- `hold_queued_at` took the CREATED line's timestamp (,085) instead of the QUEUED line's (,107).
- `feed_timeout_ms` took the orders service's 20000 instead of the feed's 25000.

Both values occur verbatim in the logs, so no deterministic check catches them.
DB-B03@final: 10/12 on both runs, up from 0/9. The retried upstream trace and the root cause are right. `payment_intent_id` and `payment_amount_cents` stayed empty: run 1 was cut off by an endpoint connection failure (SSL bad record MAC) at 180 s, and run 2 finished without finding the intent. No run ended early from repeated calls.
